history.title: Iowa adopts the State Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: House File 2304 (87th GA, 2018) authorized the Iowa Seal of Biliteracy, administered by the Iowa Department of Education for high-school graduates demonstrating proficiency in English plus one or more world languages.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Iowa's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: Iowa DOE rebrands to educate.iowa.gov domain
history.description: The Iowa Department of Education migrated its public-facing domain from educateiowa.gov to educate.iowa.gov, with redirects in place. Earlier citations against the prior domain may resolve through the redirect chain.

elPercentHistory.note: Iowa Department of Education, October 1 fall snapshot (approximately 40,000 EL students). EL identification via home language survey plus ELPA21 screener; K-12 public denominator. The 0.8 percentage-point increase over NCES's fall 2021 value (6.2%) is a modest upward continuation of the NCES trajectory. Iowa does not publish a multi-year EL table for fall 2018-2021 in directly accessible form, so methodological continuity with the prior NCES series cannot be confirmed from overlapping observations.
